steps.say: Paracetamol acute liver failure is listed for transplant when arterial pee aitch falls below seven point three after resuscitation, or when grade three or four brain failure joins creatinine above three point four with INR above six point five. These Kings College paracetamol criteria mark a liver that will not recover alone. Meet them and the referral goes the same day, since waiting for deeper coma only adds brain injury.
steps.tx: Paracetamol acute liver failure is listed for transplant when arterial **pH falls below 7.3** after resuscitation, or when grade 3 or 4 encephalopathy joins **creatinine above 3.4 mg/dL** with **INR above 6.5**. These **King's College** paracetamol criteria mark a liver that will not recover alone. Meet them and the referral goes the same day, since waiting for deeper coma only adds brain injury.

vis.alt: Hepatocyte necrosis leading to coagulopathy, brain swelling, and multiorgan failure in acute liver failure.
vis.caption: From hepatocyte necrosis to multiorgan failure. Listing cutoffs are in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: Without paracetamol, Kings College listing needs INR above six point five alone, or any three of five: age under ten or over forty, a drug or indeterminate cause, jaundice to brain failure over seven days, INR above three point five, and bilirubin above seventeen. The pattern points to older patients, slow onsets, and deep jaundice. Count the features at the bedside before calling the transplant centre.
steps.tx: Without paracetamol, **King's College** listing needs **INR above 6.5** alone, or any three of five: age **under 10 or over 40**, a drug or indeterminate cause, jaundice to encephalopathy over 7 days, INR above 3.5, and **bilirubin above 17 mg/dL**. The pattern points to older patients, slow onsets, and deep cholestasis. Count the features at the bedside before calling the transplant centre.

steps.say: N-acetylcysteine is given for paracetamol acute liver failure even when the patient presents late, and it is reasonable in non-paracetamol failure too. It restores glutathione and supports microcirculation, but it does not replace transplant assessment. Start it while the cause is still being worked out, and continue it into the transplant referral.
steps.tx: **N-acetylcysteine** is given for **paracetamol** acute liver failure even when the patient presents late, and it is reasonable in non-paracetamol failure too. It restores glutathione and supports microcirculation, but it does not replace **transplant** assessment. Start it while the aetiology is still being worked out, and continue it into the transplant referral.

steps.say: An arterial ammonia above about two hundred warns of brain swelling in acute liver failure. Management is head-up positioning, normal temperature, water removal therapy, and avoiding low sodium. Lactulose alone does not treat this swelling, though it still has its place in chronic brain fog from liver disease. Watch the pupils and the sodium together, since falling sodium swells the brain further.
steps.tx: An arterial **ammonia above about 200 micromol/L** warns of **cerebral oedema** in acute liver failure. Management is head-up positioning, normothermia, **osmotherapy**, and avoiding hyponatraemia. **Lactulose** alone does not treat this oedema, though it still has its place in chronic encephalopathy. Watch the pupils and the sodium together, since a falling sodium swells the brain further.

vis.alt: Gut ammonia bypassing the liver, astrocyte swelling, and brain swelling with flapping tremor in hepatic encephalopathy.
vis.caption: Ammonia from gut to astrocyte swelling. The ammonia threshold is in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: Acute on chronic liver failure is graded by counting failing organs on the CLIF organ failure score: liver, kidney, brain, clotting, circulation, and breathing. Prognosis is worse than a simple decompensation with the same bilirubin, because each extra failure multiplies short term death. Name the failing organs daily, since the count decides intensive care escalation and transplant discussion.
steps.tx: **Acute on chronic liver failure** is graded by counting **organ failures** on the **CLIF** organ failure score: liver, kidney, brain, coagulation, circulation, and respiration. Prognosis is worse than a simple decompensation with the same bilirubin, because each extra failure multiplies short term death. Name the failing organs daily, since the count decides ICU escalation and transplant talk.

steps.say: Variceal bleeding is treated with a vessel tightening drug, terlipressin or octreotide, plus an antibiotic, plus early endoscopy. A restrictive transfusion target near seven grams per decilitre is used unless the patient is bleeding out, since overfilling raises portal pressure and rebleeding. Balloon tamponade bridges the gap only when endoscopy cannot control the bleed.
steps.tx: **Variceal bleeding** is treated with a **vasoactive drug**, terlipressin or octreotide, plus an antibiotic, plus early **endoscopy**. A restrictive transfusion target near **7 g/dL** is used unless the patient is exsanguinating, since overfilling raises portal pressure and rebleeding. Balloon tamponade bridges the gap only when endoscopy cannot control the bleed.

vis.alt: Balloon tamponade tube with oesophageal and gastric balloons, ports, and position across the gastro-oesophageal junction.
vis.caption: Balloon tamponade as rescue when endoscopy fails. Balloon volumes printed on the drawing are not the lesson; drugs, antibiotics and endoscopy timing are in the text (StewardMD).

steps.say: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis is treated with a third generation cephalosporin, and albumin one point five grams per kilo on day one plus one gram per kilo on day three when creatinine is above one, urea above thirty, or bilirubin above four. Albumin protects the kidney and improves survival in this high risk group. Tap the ascites before antibiotics whenever the diagnosis is suspected.
steps.tx: **Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis** is treated with a **third generation cephalosporin**, and **albumin** 1.5 g/kg on day 1 plus 1 g/kg on day 3 when **creatinine is above 1 mg/dL**, urea above 30 mg/dL, or bilirubin above 4 mg/dL. Albumin protects the kidney and improves survival in this high risk group. Tap the ascites before antibiotics whenever the diagnosis is suspected.

rows: Creatinine above 1, urea above 30, bilirubin above 4

steps.say: High volume plasma exchange can improve transplant free survival in acute liver failure. It is a bridge, not a cure: it buys time for recovery or for a graft, and it is done in a transplant centre. Standard care and the listing decision continue alongside, since exchange alone does not remove the need for a new liver.
